subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Internal Controls and Segregation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Internal Controls and Segregation usable.

hook.text: One person handles the money, approves payments, and reconciles the books. That's an invitation to steal.

buildup.text: Segregation of duties splits critical functions so no one person controls an entire process end-to-end.

discovery.text: Internal controls like dual signatures, access restrictions, and mandatory vacations catch and prevent fraud.

twist.text: Small companies can't always segregate duties. They need compensating controls like management review.

climax.text: Strong controls make fraud harder, not impossible. They raise the effort needed and the risk of getting caught.

punchline.text: No one person handles everything. That's the first rule.

quiz.question: What is segregation of duties?
options: Splitting critical functions so no one person controls everything
Requiring all employees to work remotely
